items.title: China fossil may reveal first amphibian to live entirely at sea 237m years ago
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.

items.title: Court rejects Nevada ranchers' demand to swiftly remove excess wild horses
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: On October 29, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit upheld a decision favoring federal officials regarding wild horses. Ranchers Colvin & Son, LLC and Stone Cabin Ranch challenged the Bureau of Land Management's Gather Plans for lacking a specific timetable. The court ruled that the Wild Free Roaming Horses and Burros Act does not require a fixed timeframe for removals.

Furthermore, traffic patterns will be adjusted to reroute through-traffic away from Delhi.
